But add aliases for backward compatibility.

Fix: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/52430
pr_comments: I've opened https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/52467 in the same spirit of this PR. It renames `text_area_tag` to `textarea_tag` and `rich_text_area_tag` to `rich_textarea_tag`, while preserving backward compatibility with aliases.

I guess it would make sense to deprecate `check_box` and output a warning at some point. And then removing it in a later version. 

Does Ruby on Rails have some kind of guideline or recommendation when to alias or when to deprecate a method? And how long to keep the old version?
This isn't something worth deprecating, it's a simple alias.
This is perhaps one of the most monumental changes to Rails in forever! 😆 Kudos.

This puts generators in an akward place where they need to handle both variants if they want to properly support both old and new rails versions. https://github.com/rails/tailwindcss-rails/pull/418 ~Would it make sense to still return the old version from `field_type`?~ Nope, `field_type` is obviously used to generate what ends up in the generated file so having that return the old value would also generate old method names. Not sure what would be an appropriate backwards compatible change, if there is any.

Maybe it's fine? It looks like that whole thing is undocumented actually. I don't know enough about generators (zero to none actually) to be able to tell.

issue_context.title: Can we have a checkbox alias?
issue_context.body:
It is certainly acceptable to refer to checkboxes as two words: "Check Box". But more often, they are referred to as "Checkbox" (one word):
* HTML: [input `type="checkbox"`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox)
* Wikipedia: [Checkbox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkbox)
* Nielson Norman Group: [Checkboxes](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/checkboxes-design-guidelines/)

For backwards compatibility, it makes sense to continue supporting `check_box` Form Helper, but I propose adding an alias (or making `check_box` the alias), so that our forms can refer to them as simply "checkbox", without the underscore.

The classes/methods that I think should be aliased are:
* [ActionView::Helpers::FormHelper#check_box](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/19eebf6d33dd15a0172e3ed2481bec57a89a2404/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/form_helper.rb#L1343)
* [ActionView::Helpers::FormBuilder#check_box](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/19eebf6d33dd15a0172e3ed2481bec57a89a2404/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/form_helper.rb#L2468)
* [ActionView::Helpers::FormBuilder#collection_check_boxes](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/19eebf6d33dd15a0172e3ed2481bec57a89a2404/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/form_options_helper.rb#L908)
* [ActionView::Helpers::FormOptionsHelper#collection_check_boxes](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/19eebf6d33dd15a0172e3ed2481bec57a89a2404/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/form_options_helper.rb#L782)
* [ActionView::Helpers::FormTagHelper#check_box_tag](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/19eebf6d33dd15a0172e3ed2481bec57a89a2404/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/form_tag_helper.rb#L455)
* [ActionView::Helpers::Tags::CheckBox](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/def0397e595c503099e3c10bd811d5d9e3613b38/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/tags/check_box.rb)
* [ActionView::Helpers::Tags::CollectionCheckBoxes and CheckBoxBuilder#check_box](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/def0397e595c503099e3c10bd811d5d9e3613b38/actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/tags/collection_check_boxes.rb)

If this proposal is acceptable, I can draft a PR to make this change. Let me know what you think.
comments: I think an alias is good, but @dhh might have a strong opinion about this.
Yes, I'm fine with an alias. But let's indeed make checkbox_tag the new primary and check_box_tag an eternal alias to the new name.
I agree. I have always found this annoying.
